meta.notes: Torah #86 ('Pos'im bo ps'ia ketana') is a short teaching of 12 lines. Of the 5 total edges with reference===86, only 2 are bechina (IDs 349 and 3005); the remaining 3 (IDs 912, 1568, 1671) are eitza. The bechina subgraph yields exactly 2 connected components, each with 2 nodes. No merging is possible or warranted: the two pairs inhabit distinct essential natures — Package 1 is the identity of Shabbat as truth/support, Package 2 is the identity of charity as the solar empowering force. The connection between the two packages is eitza: the sun-charity PRODUCES power for the legs (cause-and-effect), while truth IS the third leg (shared nature). No evil mirror exists in the bechina dataset for this Torah, reflecting the teaching's positive-only arc: it describes restoration of holy walking on Shabbat and the two forces that enable it.

packages.label: שַׁבָּת וֶאֱמֶת
packages.reason: שבת (Shabbat) and אמת (Truth) share a single essential nature in this Torah: they are both the same supportive, stabilizing force that enables a person to walk in God's ways. The Torah states explicitly 'שַׁבָּת הוּא בְחִינַת אֱמֶת' — Shabbat IS an aspect of truth — grounded in the Talmud's observation that even an unlearned person is afraid to lie on Shabbat (masechet Demai ch. 4). This is not a causal claim (Shabbat does not produce truth) but a statement of essential identity: they are the same stabilizing quality. The Talmud further states 'קֻשְׁטָא קָאֵי' — truth stands firm (on two legs; Shabbat 104), and that truth is itself a 'third leg' (רגל שלישי), the support (סעד) that a beginner-walker needs. Shabbat and truth are two names for the same supportive, anti-deception, stabilizing ground beneath the feet of the person who is just beginning to walk in God's ways.

packages.label: צְדָקָה וְשֶׁמֶשׁ
packages.reason: צדקה (charity) and שמש (the sun) share a single essential nature: they are both the same luminous, empowering, life-giving radiance that gives strength to movement and walking. The Torah states 'וּצְדָקָה הוּא בְחִינוֹת שֶׁמֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מַלְאָכִי ג): שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה' — charity IS an aspect of the sun, based on Malachi's 'a sun of righteousness.' This identity is not metaphor but ontological equivalence: the charitable act radiates the same essential quality as solar light. Within the Torah's framework, two solar instances are distinguished — the present-day sun (corresponding to weekday charity) and the future sun of Shabbat-charity (כאור שבעת הימים — 'as the light of the seven days'), but both are the same sun-nature. Charity and the sun are two names for the same luminous, energizing, walking-enabling force.

stats.note_on_small_components: Both components are 2-node pairs. No merging is warranted: the two pairs are connected to each other only via eitza (the sun-charity GIVES POWER to the legs/walking — a causal relationship), not via bechina (shared nature). Shabbat=Truth is the stabilizing supportive identity; Charity=Sun is the luminous empowering identity. These are two distinct essential natures in this Torah.
stats.note_on_evil_mirror: No evil-polarity bechina edges exist in the dataset for Torah #86. The teaching has no explicit evil-side bechina cluster — its arc is entirely positive: restoring the power of walking in God's ways on Shabbat via truth and charity. The Chitzonim (external forces) are named as the opposing force but carry no bechina-typed edges in this Torah.
